Cover illustration for a lifehacker.dev Hacks article.

TITLE — typeset this exact headline, large, high-contrast, in the vertical middle 60% of the frame. No other words, no byline, no watermark, no logo:
Your first React app with Vite: components, props, and a useState counter

SUBJECT
Scaffold a React app with Vite, render JSX, manage state with useState, pass props between components, and decode the two errors everyone hits first.

NOTES
Every React tutorial promises to demystify the framework. Most of them spend nine paragraphs on the philosophy of declarative UI before you type a single command. This is the other kind: four commands to a running app, one counter that counts, and the two errors you will hit on the way — left in, because hitting them is the actual lesson. You need Node installed (any current LTS). Check it first: If those print version numbers, you're set. If is "command not found," install it from nodejs.org an

ART DIRECTION
Trace Bloom: dark field #05070d over #0b1020, lattice #1b2b44, signal #22d3ee, heat #f472b6, ink #eaf6ff, accent #22d3ee. Diagrammatic, high-contrast, cinematic 3:2 landscape. Draw the concrete apparatus this article is about — not a generic circuit board, robot, brain, or rocket. No faces. No UI chrome. No stock-tech collage. The still frame must read at 300px.
